source_text: Presentations and properties of algebraic stacks

<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a groupoid in algebraic spaces.
If <MATH_0002> are flat and locally of finite presentation,
then the quotient stack <MATH_0003> is an algebraic stack, see
Criteria for Representability, Theorem
<REF_0001>.
In this section we study what properties of <MATH_0004>
imply for the algebraic stack <MATH_0005>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a groupoid in algebraic spaces such that
<MATH_0002> are flat and locally of finite presentation.
Consider the algebraic stack <MATH_0003> (see above).
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0004> is separated, then
<MATH_0005> is separated.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0006>, <MATH_0007> are separated, then <MATH_0008> is separated.
<STRUCT_0004> If <MATH_0009> is locally quasi-finite, then <MATH_0010>
is quasi-DM.
<STRUCT_0005> If <MATH_0011> are locally quasi-finite, then
<MATH_0012> is quasi-DM.
<STRUCT_0006> If <MATH_0013> is proper, then <MATH_0014> is separated.
<STRUCT_0007> If <MATH_0015> are proper and <MATH_0016> is separated, then
<MATH_0017> is separated.

Observe that the morphism <MATH_0001> is surjective, flat, and
locally of finite presentation by
Criteria for Representability, Lemma
<REF_0001>.
Hence the same is true for <MATH_0002>.
We have the cartesian diagram
<MATH_0003>

Thus we see that <MATH_0004> has one of the properties listed in
Properties of Stacks, Section
<REF_0003>
if and only if the morphism <MATH_0005> does, see
Properties of Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0004>.
This explains why (1), (3), and (5) are true.
The condition in (2) implies <MATH_0006> is separated
hence (2) follows from (1).
The condition in (4) implies the condition in (3)
hence (4) follows from (3).
The condition in (6) implies the condition in (5)
by Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0005>
